items.title: Asheville council approves zoning changes to expand housing options
items.summary: Asheville's council approved changes allowing duplexes and accessory dwelling units more widely, as part of a rewrite of the city's unified development ordinance.

items.title: ROAD to Nowhere: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act is now law
items.summary: Congress passed the ROAD to Housing Act with veto-proof margins, 85-5 in the Senate and 358-32 in the House, tying federal housing funding to local zoning reform and streamlining environmental review.

items.title: Governor Sherrill, NJEDA and NJ TRANSIT Initiate New Transit-Oriented Development Projects
items.summary: NJEDA and NJ TRANSIT issued a request for qualifications and proposals to redevelop a site at Linden Train Station, with proposals due September 23, 2026.

items.title: MORE HOUSING, FASTER: Governor Newsom signs historic housing affordability reforms
items.summary: California signed a housing affordability package the state estimates will cut affordable construction costs by $60,000 to $70,000 per unit through One-Stop Shop financing and impact fee changes.

items.title: City Selects Pair Of Mixed-Use Buildings For West Englewood
items.summary: Chicago picked two mixed-use buildings for West Englewood through a city RFP, selling the lots for $1 each against an $18 million total project cost.

items.title: The ROAD To Housing Act: Congress's Down Payment On The American Dream
items.summary: Analysis of the bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act and which of its supply-side provisions are likely to move production.

items.title: Request for Proposals: Downtown Multifamily Development
items.summary: Blaine, Washington released an RFP for a downtown multifamily redevelopment, issued June 8 with proposals due July 8, 2026.

items.title: ArtPhilly Spreads Creativity Throughout The City Where America Was Born
items.summary: Philadelphia's first ArtPhilly festival ran May 27 to July 2, 2026, with citywide projects made by and with local artists across music, theater, dance and visual art.

items.title: FY 2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity: Pilot Program for Transit-Oriented Development Planning
items.summary: FTA made about $28.5 million available for FY 2026 TOD planning grants, with applications due July 10, 2026.

items.title: MPAC breaks ground on $65M expansion, launching arts center and major theater restoration
items.summary: The Mayo Performing Arts Center broke ground on a $65 million expansion pairing a new arts center with a restoration of its historic theater.

items.title: Stevens Center Phase 2 design plans revealed
items.summary: The university revealed phase two design plans for the Stevens Center, its downtown Winston-Salem performance venue.

items.title: Small Lots, Big Impact: Speaker Menin Proposes Reforms To Unlock Up To 35,000 Units Of Housing On Small Lots
items.summary: Speaker Menin proposed construction code reforms the Council says could yield up to 35,000 apartments on small, irregularly shaped lots across the five boroughs.

items.title: E Street Transit-Oriented Development: Disposition and Development Agreement
items.summary: The San Diego MTS board authorized a disposition and development agreement with Bayview Family Housing for the E Street TOD, whose affordable component is being delivered by Eden Housing.

items.title: Lakewood, Colorado's Zoning Vote Is A Housing Affordability Bellwether

items.title: Public-private partnership yields luxury apartments, new infrastructure in Oregon's 'Silicon Forest'
items.summary: Wood Partners' 594-unit Astral and Revel by Alta in Hillsboro, built in cooperation with the city, won a 2026 CoStar Impact Award for Portland multifamily development of the year.

items.title: Report: Every US State is Unaffordable for the Lowest-income Households
items.summary: The 2026 Gap report finds a shortage of 7.2 million homes for the lowest-income renters, 35 available homes per 100 extremely low-income households, and 74% of those renters spending over half their income on housing.

items.title: The Housing Policy Inflection Point: What Will Change In 2026

items.title: Guide to the Seattle Building Emissions Performance Standard
items.summary: Seattle's standard requires most buildings over 20,000 sq ft to reach net zero emissions between 2041 and 2050; buildings account for 40% of the city's greenhouse gas emissions.

items.title: LACMA Announces Plans Toward 2026 Grand Public Opening of the New David Geffen Galleries

items.title: A New Cultural Landmark: Lucas Museum of Narrative Art Set to Open in 2026
items.summary: The Lucas Museum turns a former parking lot into galleries, theaters and landscaped public space, with commitments on local hiring and inclusive design.

items.title: 2026 California Legislative Preview

items.title: 2026 Green Building Outlook: From Policy to Proof

items.title: BIG Reveals Design for Tennessee Performing Arts Center in Nashville

items.title: Building Decarbonization: Top 10 Insights from the ULI Net Zero Imperative
